en: Coming!
Mama's at work.
Strangers can't come in the house,
I was told. So, bye-bye.
note: Cut kept at the JP break: 'Strangers can't come in the house, / I was told.'

en: Sorry! Later, okay?
Oh, it's mister! Hello.
Nobody can come in the house, Mama
told me. So, bye-bye. See you!
Come again, okay?
'Mister,' huh
. Nice to meet you.
I've just moved to London.
I see. Nice to meet you, Jill.
Oh, it's mister! Bye-bye.
Oh, it's mister! Good morning.
Jill's mama gets up really early, you know.
It's dark now. You should be getting home.
Nuh-uh, it's okay. Mama doesn't get home
note: As required by report 105 (followed by #8430 'till after dark either.').

en: Is your mama at work?
Well, big brother's name is
Nice to meet you, Jill.
I'm sorry, Jill
Your mama will be heartbroken
Must I really go this far
I curse my own fate
My master, ask anything of me...
Ow, that hurts! What on earth is this?
There are ugly bruises all over me.
, my master, is it not?
note: Servant mode (M2#0 rule): NAME + ', my master, is it not?'

en: What is your wish? Do tell me.
I'd tumbled out of bed this morning.
How unladylike. My roots must be showing.
Did you want something of me?
Greeting beautiful ladies is a habit of
mine, you see. Have I offended you?
My, what an amusing thing to say.
I don't mind at all.
I'm Henrietta. A pleasure to meet you.
Well then, I'm sure we'll meet again.
Oh my, you look rather idle.
You're out early, I see. Is it work?
Men have it hard. Well, good day to you.
Good morning. How are you today?
As for me, I'm just as you see.
I've nothing to do again today,
so I'll pass the time at the usual jewelry shop.
Um... Have we met somewhere before?
No, this is our first meeting. My name is
With beautiful ladies, I always make a
point of introducing myself, you see.
Really? What an amusing man.
My name is Henrietta.
Delighted to meet you, charming sir.
The pleasure is all mine, I assure you.
If we meet again, do say hello.
We meet again! It must be fate.
New friends are always welcome.
note: JP row ends in 、; ended as a sentence since #8537 starts a new line and a new thought.

en: I'd like to invite you to my next tea party.
Please do come.
My, to run into you in a place like this,
how lucky!
I've been bored to death all day today.
If only I'd met you sooner.
I wanted you to keep me company.
My, how rare! A gentleman in this shop.
Is it a present for someone?
Good day, lovely lady.
And you? Looking for new jewelry?
No, this shop is on my daily rounds.
There's nothing to do at home,
so I come here every day. A feast for the eyes.
Not that I mean to buy anything.
But the owner can't complain, you see.
I have the Baron behind me.
...I see.
I'm Henrietta. The Baron's mistress.
At least, that's what people say.
(Some humans are strange indeed...)
Good day. We meet again.
Looking for some new jewelry, perhaps?
